root_cause.text: The dpaa2-switch IRQ handler used a 16-bit if_id from the hardware status register as an index into ethsw->ports[] without checking that it was less than sw_attr.num_ifs, allowing an out-of-bounds access when hardware reports an invalid port ID.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (if_id >= ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs) { dev_err(dev, "Invalid if_id %d in IRQ status\n", if_id); goto out; }` immediately before `port_priv = ethsw->ports[if_id];`, and the CVE notes that `if_id` comes from the upper 16 bits of the IRQ status register while `ports[]` is only allocated with `sw_attr.num_ifs` elements.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check in the switch IRQ handler to reject invalid interface IDs before indexing the ports array.
intent_record.what: The handler now extracts `if_id` from `status` and adds a bounds check against `ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs`; if the ID is invalid, it logs an error with `dev_err()` and jumps to `out` instead of indexing `ethsw->ports[if_id]`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the IRQ thread from accessing the ports array with an out-of-range interface ID taken from the interrupt status, avoiding invalid memory access and handling malformed or unexpected IRQ status safely.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check in the switch IRQ handler to reject invalid interface IDs before indexing the ports array.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the vulnerability root cause: it adds a bounds check in the IRQ handler before using the hardware-provided if_id to index ethsw->ports[], preventing out-of-bounds access from invalid port IDs.

candidates.rationale: This statement directly indexes the ports array using the hardware-derived if_id without any prior bounds check, which can cause an out-of-bounds access when the switch reports an invalid interface ID.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the hardware-derived 16-bit if_id directly as an index into ethsw->ports[] without a preceding bounds check against sw_attr.num_ifs, which matches the reported out-of-bounds access vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the IRQ handler. The code extracts a 16-bit interface ID from the status register with `if_id = (status & 0xFFFF0000) >> 16;` and then immediately indexes `ethsw->ports[if_id];` with no bounds check against `ethsw->sw_attr.num_ifs`. This matches the root cause: an invalid hardware-reported port ID can cause out-of-bounds access. The fix is not present here because there is no validation such as `if_id < num_ifs` or a guard before dereferencing `port_priv->netdev`; the handler uses the index directly.
